Rather, in humility value others above yourselves, not looking to your own interests but each of you to the interests of the others."* - This suggests that even when you believe you deserve recognition (like a raise), prioritizing the well-being of others (your boss, team, or organization) reflects Christ-like humility. 2. **Trusting God’s Timing (Proverbs 3:5-6, Psalm 37:5)** - *"Commit your way to the Lord; trust in him, and he will act."* If Mark feels God has called him for the raise, he might ask: *Is this about my worth, or God’s plan?* Humility could mean trusting God’s timing, even if it doesn’t align with immediate expectations. 3. **Servant Leadership (Mark 10:42-45, Matthew 20:25-28)** - Jesus taught that true greatness comes from serving others. If Mark’s boss has different priorities, humility might involve asking: *How can I contribute to the team’s success, even if it doesn’t directly benefit me?* 4. **Contentment (Hebrews 13:5, 1 Timothy 6:6-8)** - *"God has said, ‘Never will I leave you; never will I forsake you.’ So we can confidently say, ‘The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid.’"* Humility in this context could mean finding satisfaction in God’s provision rather than earthly validation. ### **Reflection Questions for Mark:** - *Is my desire for the raise rooted in pride (needing to prove myself) or a genuine need to provide for my family?* - *How can I honor my boss and the organization’s mission, even if my personal goals aren’t met?* - *What would Jesus do in this situation? Would He demand recognition or serve with humility?* ### **Possible Responses (Not "Right" or "Wrong" but Theological Frameworks):** - **Option 1: Humble Acceptance** - *"Lord, I trust Your plan. If this raise isn’t part of Your timing, help me to serve faithfully and patiently wait."* - This aligns with Philippians 4:11 (*"I have learned to be content..."*) and could foster deeper trust in God. - **Option 2: Humble Advocacy** - *"I respect my boss’s decision, but I’d love to discuss how I can contribute more to justify future opportunities."* - This balances humility with proactive engagement (Proverbs 11:15: *"The righteous flourish like the palm tree..."*). - **Option 3: Humble Reflection** - *"Maybe God is teaching me patience or dependence on Him through this. I’ll pray for wisdom and clarity."* ### **Why This Matters for Christians:** Humility isn’t about self-deprecation but about aligning our desires with God’s will. It’s about loving others (including our boss) more than ourselves (1 Corinthians 13:4-5). If Mark’s heart is right—seeking God’s glory over personal gain—then his actions (even in disappointment) can reflect Christ.
